fault.explanation: reload({ resolveProjectTrust }) performed the untrusted bootstrap extension load (loadProjectTrustExtensions(), which already forces settingsManager.setProjectTrusted(false)) and then hard-coded projectTrusted = false instead of consulting the supplied resolver. The trust resolver was never called, so an approved project never received its project-scoped settings/extensions/packages and no extension project_trust handler could ever run.

repair.change: const projectTrusted = await options.resolveProjectTrust({ extensionsResult: preTrustExtensions });
repair.notes: One-line minimal change: the resolver is invoked exactly once, is awaited before SettingsManager.setProjectTrusted() and the subsequent trusted resource pass, and receives the untrusted bootstrap LoadExtensionsResult produced by loadProjectTrustExtensions(). No other production code touched.

claims.claim: Policy explicitly allows project resources after a true decision.
claims.citation: packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts:450-455 (DefaultResourceLoader.reload) passing the resolver result to SettingsManager.setProjectTrusted, consumed by packages/coding-agent/src/core/package-manager.ts:1746 and resource-loader.ts:1095,1109
claims.evidence: regression.mjs scenario 1: resolver returns true -> project extension is loaded and settingsManager.isProjectTrusted() === true.

claims.claim: Policy denies project resources after a false decision.
claims.evidence: regression.mjs scenario 2: resolver returns false -> only the user extension is loaded, project extension never loaded, trust state stays false.

claims.claim: The resolver must observe an untrusted bootstrap result.
claims.citation: packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts:435-441 (loadProjectTrustExtensions forces setProjectTrusted(false) and reloads) followed by the resolver call at line 453
claims.evidence: regression.mjs asserts the resolver input carries the user-only bootstrap extensionsResult while settingsManager.isProjectTrusted() === false.

claims.claim: Call the resolver once and preserve its asynchronous ordering.
claims.evidence: regression.mjs asserts resolverCalls === 1 and event ordering: packageManager.resolve(trusted=false) -> trustResolver.start -> trustResolver.end (after a 25ms async gap) -> packageManager.resolve(trusted=true).

validation.notes: Ran from the workspace root with Node v24.14.0 (TypeScript stripping + --experimental-vm-modules); exit code 0, output 'resource-loader project trust regression: all scenarios passed'. The script loads the real packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts through .prale-eval/subject.mjs loadModule() with hand-written boundary fakes for chalk, ../config.ts, ../utils/paths.ts, ../utils/text.ts, ./event-bus.ts, ./extensions/loader.ts, ./footer-data-provider.ts, ./package-manager.ts, ./prompt-templates.ts, ./settings-manager.ts, ./skills.ts, ./source-info.ts and ./timings.ts; the fake package manager mirrors DefaultPackageManager by withholding project-scoped resources unless settingsManager.isProjectTrusted(), and every scenario uses non-existent fixture paths so no filesystem writes or network access occur. Three scenarios are asserted with node:assert/strict (no printed-success shortcuts): (1) resolver resolves true after a 25ms async gap -> resolver called exactly once, its input is the untrusted, user-only bootstrap LoadExtensionsResult, and after reload the project and user extensions are both present with the user extension loaded exactly once; (2) resolver resolves false -> project extension never loaded and trust state remains false; (3) reload() without a resolveProjectTrust option -> resolver not invoked and a previously saved trusted/untrusted decision still gates project resources. Fault re-check performed locally: reverting the repaired line back to 'const projectTrusted = false;' makes the script exit 1 with 'AssertionError: trusted decision: project trust resolver must be consulted exactly once (0 !== 1)'; restoring the fix returns exit 0. Limitation: the repository has no installed node_modules, so the upstream vitest suite (test/resource-loader.test.ts, which asserts the same contract) and any tsc typecheck could not be executed in this sandbox; validation therefore relies on the standalone Node regression described above.
